public_rationale: Both parts are supported. A September 2025 Senate hearing account records two chatbot-associated suicide reports, and a December 2025 complaint alleges a chatbot connection to a murder-suicide. Wikipedia's January 14, 2026 revision already collected these and additional cases. This establishes several reported associations and Wikipedia coverage before Marcus's post. It does not establish that chatbots caused the deaths.
limitations: The complaint and hearing account contain allegations, not judicial findings of causation.
The historical Wikipedia revision also records OpenAI's competing account of the Raine case. That dispute does not contradict the existence of reported associations.
The evidence establishes that Wikipedia was tracking cases by January 14, 2026, without identifying its first tracking date.

our_interpretation: Read 'several' as at least three distinct reported deaths, with suicide and homicide both represented.
Reported association means a publicly alleged connection with chatbot interactions. It does not require proof that a chatbot caused a death.
Read 'by now' cumulatively through January 15, 2026. The surrounding account begins with deaths reported in 2023, so the target period starts in that year.
Wikipedia tracking means an identifiable article collecting such cases existed by the post date. 'Enough that' does not require evidence of editors' motives.
criteria.support_condition: By January 15, 2026, public records described at least three distinct chatbot-associated deaths, including suicide and homicide, and a dated Wikipedia revision collected such cases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable historical records establish that the reported cases did not meet the threshold or include both categories, or that Wikipedia began collecting these cases only after January 15, 2026.
